latest_release.body:
# v0.3.4 — Faster startup and atomic initialization

Release scope: **faster CLI startup and atomic initial schema/FTS creation, with preserved retrieval outputs**. Startup acceptance includes an explicitly reviewed resource tradeoff; the complete fresh comparison passes its integrity and output-equivalence checks. Publication is gated on the exact release commit's nine-job CI and verified package/public-installer workflow.

The confirmed improvements are new-archive construction and actual CLI help/version startup. This release uses exact source A, with its rejected dense-project ranking experiment excluded. Existing archives retain schema 3, source addresses, citations, token budgets and the public `MemoryBook` class.

## What changes

- Initial schema and FTS creation share one immediate transaction. The empty/schema checks are repeated after acquiring the lock, complete trigger statements stay intact, and a schema setup failure rolls back. The subsequent covering-index and connection PRAGMA steps keep their prior boundaries.
- Package and command metadata load without eagerly importing the archive, transcript importers and client/capture machinery. Explicit `MemoryBook` import still loads the complete API; class identity, star import, type hints and CLI class overrides remain covered by tests.
- Native FTS candidates retain narrow metadata only within the same recall, removing a redundant metadata read while preserving complete directory validation. Custom factories/connections and constrained or uninspectable SQLite limits retain the previous query path. Python 3.10 takes that conservative metadata fallback.

## Measured startup gains and retained costs

The unique [prospective confirmation](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43598913606) completed all **480 original samples and 960 events**, with four AB/BA/BA/AB rounds on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12, fixed MCP 1.30.0 and Pydantic 2.14.3. Each source contributes forty fresh samples per boundary. No first sample, outlier or failed result was removed, and no timing was repeated.

Times below are milliseconds, **v0.3.3 → v0.3.4**. Negative changes mean less elapsed time.

| Boundary | Median | Median change | p95 | p95 change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New empty-archive constructor | 24.518 → 4.164 | -83.02% | 27.374 → 6.358 | -76.77% |
| Real CLI --help process | 102.903 → 48.750 | -52.63% | 104.104 → 49.547 | -52.41% |
| Real CLI --version process | 101.346 → 47.479 | -53.15% | 103.116 → 48.259 | -53.20% |
| Full API import, including MemoryBook | 33.506 → 33.920 | +1.24% | 33.822 → 34.433 | +1.81% |
| Existing empty-archive constructor | 0.640 → 0.632 | -1.23% | 0.668 → 0.666 | -0.30% |
| Official SDK transport/server initialization | 627.601 → 620.104 | -1.19% | 632.233 → 624.837 | -1.17% |

New-archive median falls by **20.354 ms**; help and version medians fall by **54.153 ms** and **53.867 ms**. Constructor timing excludes Python launch, import and evidence validation; CLI timing covers the actual complete fresh process; MCP timing ends at successful initialization. These boundaries are separate. All three primary percentage/absolute targets and all six secondary guards pass their preregistered thresholds.

Complete API import becomes slower by **0.414 ms median / 0.611 ms p95**. Existing-archive whole-helper system CPU rises **18.646175 → 21.120575 ms**, or **+2.474400 ms / +13.270282%**, in every round. It is the one pooled resource increase requiring review. Whole-helper wall mean rises **1.233748 ms / 0.889110%**, and saved user+system CPU rises **1.228375 ms**. The existing-archive constructor's own median and p95 do not regress. No syscall/component trace identifies the exact cause; the increase is not dismissed as noise or attributed to the new-schema transaction.

Two independent saved-evidence reviews support accepting this bounded tradeoff for startup scope. The [explicit startup decision](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-decision.json) records that acceptance separately from the unchanged original **`accepted:false` and workflow `failure`**. Every original resource flag and all **6 pooled / 26 round timing increases plus 9 pooled / 27 round resource increases** remain available. Kernel child RSS records and sampled live MCP resources do not establish isolated product-memory savings.

[Full saved-result review](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1-local-audit/review.md) · [Independent resource review](../round6-startup-resource-review.md) · [Original report](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1/report.json.gz) · [Original plan](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-plan.json).

## Retrieval evidence and scope

A's balanced development experiment completed **22,988 calls / 11,494 complete output pairs / 45,976 events** with all complete non-timing outputs equal. Recall improvements were roughly **1%**, insufficient to advance to the original **10% aggregate / 15% public native / 10% actual MCP p95** targets. That four-round formal recall matrix was **not run or accepted**. B regressed public native p95 approximately **19–29%** and actual MCP p95 **23.9246%**; it remains excluded with its entire experiment preserved.

The exact A runtime also matches all **2,304 historical Hotpot256 complete outputs** against v0.3.3, independently audited against **4,608 events**. These are compatibility results, not new retrieval-quality gains. Historical C7 and optional Q2 results retain their original versions and measured boundaries.

## Complete fresh component comparison

The sole [comparison run 43601518020](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43601518020) finished all eight stages: **6,912 retrieval/search calls, 42 quality cells, 13,824 search ledger events and 1,280 separately recorded ai-memory page reads**. All **1,536 native + 768 component complete-output pairs** match v0.3.3; only latency fields are removed for the payload comparison. All 28 original result files match immutable result commit `3e6e492422705feda61b9c967d0a07dd7766dd72`. The [saved-result audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-local-audit.json) reconstructs the original assessment and Markdown exactly, without new product calls.

The same original **256 IDs** exclude all **896 historical IDs with zero overlap**. A unit fixture's manifest-path isolation failure is retained, along with its full ordinary-CI failure logs. The registered [fixture-only recovery](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-comparison-fixture-recovery-addendum.json) preserves all IDs/content hashes and all measurement/packing/adapter logic. It corrects the fixture and records the recovery through separate evaluator, binding and manifest commits before first scoring.

At the common `cl100k_base` 1,024-token whole-block projection, the complete result is:

| Component | Annotation recall | Complete evidence | Packed-context MRR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Book v0.3.3 | 75.93% | 53.12% | 0.8556 |
| Book v0.3.4 | 75.93% | 53.12% | 0.8556 |
| claude-mem 15.18.1 FTS | 70.60% | 48.05% | 0.8060 |
| ai-memory v3.4.5 hybrid | 77.87% | 57.42% | 0.8279 |
| billion-context locked kernel | 80.94% | 60.55% | 0.8481 |

Book exceeds claude-mem's annotation recall and completeness in all six tokenizer/cap cells and has the highest packed-context MRR among the four component implementations in all six. Ai-memory has higher recall and completeness in all six; billion has higher recall in all six and higher completeness at 1,024/2,048 tokens. Book's small 512-token completeness advantage over billion and all per-question losses remain visible. The seven-question low-overlap group also remains: Book completes 0/7, claude-mem 1/7, and ai-memory/billion 2/7 at 512 cl100k tokens. This is **no new retrieval-quality gain against v0.3.3 and no universal competitor lead**.

Fresh timings are descriptive and use a fixed sequential stage order. Five of six native p95 cells increase by **0.23–2.92%**, while o200k/512 decreases **3.39%**; all six native means increase **0.136–3.494%**. Component search p95 increases **3.517899 → 3.582246 ms**, about **1.83%**. Native sampled setup/query RSS increases **547.41 → 551.45 MiB / 533.12 → 537.18 MiB**; component setup wall increases **840.940 → 843.362 ms**. The larger Book native response payload, all repetitions, setup phases, RSS, storage and packing costs remain in the full results. These observations are not dismissed as noise and do not establish a causal recall change from this stage order.

**Provenance clarification beside the [unaltered automatic report](../../benchmarks/results/round6-comparison-43601518020-1/report.md):** its historical renderer text needs two qualifications. Original v1 source/evaluator/assets preceded selection; recovery v2 was frozen after the original selection and before the first scoring. Its historical reference to an ABBA recall release gate does not describe v0.3.4 acceptance: the original 10%/15%/10% recall formal matrix was not run or passed. This release uses the separate prospective startup confirmation. [Recovery freeze audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-recovery-freeze-audit.json) · [Full current comparison guide](../comparison.md) · [Independent fresh review](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-independent-review.json).

These results measure supplied-source evidence on one public answerable cohort, not generated answers, hallucination or abstention, private conversational transfer or whole products. Component API boundaries and setup work differ; no whole-product speed/ingestion/memory ratio follows. Sampled worker-plus-descendant RSS includes the evaluator and dataset, may double-count shared pages and is a lower bound. The original raw tables, source hashes and every adverse result are preserved.

## Release identity and publication gates

The approved publication runtime is **`f361d2bf64a4e1088cbd5cff6ffdaf19aa15e7f1b7ea1de4577d7a488d2ac242`**, byte-identical to source `df35007c29e4af61dd96146232fe4651cfc74391`. The [separate release decision](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-release-decision.json) preserves the earlier startup decision's historical `publication_approved:false`, the original automatic startup `accepted:false`, the rejected B result and the unpassed recall goals.

The [publication workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/workflows/release.yml) requires the exact final source commit to have all nine CI jobs pass, match `main` and `release/v0.3.4`, and match the approved runtime. It builds and independently installs the wheel and sdist, checks runtime/reader/installer bytes, publishes seven checksummed assets as a normal non-prerelease release, verifies Latest, then installs through the real public URL with default MCP/client extras. Public completion and its verification receipt are recorded after that workflow succeeds; the source-level approval is not itself a claim that those later steps already ran.

- Native FTS candidates retain narrow metadata only within the same recall, removing a redundant metadata read while preserving complete directory validation. Custom factories/connections and constrained or uninspectable SQLite limits retain the previous query path. Python 3.10 takes that conservative metadata fallback.

## Measured startup gains and retained costs

The unique [prospective confirmation](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43598913606) completed all **480 original samples and 960 events**, with four AB/BA/BA/AB rounds on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12, fixed MCP 1.30.0 and Pydantic 2.14.3. Each source contributes forty fresh samples per boundary. No first sample, outlier or failed result was removed, and no timing was repeated.

Times below are milliseconds, **v0.3.3 → v0.3.4**. Negative changes mean less elapsed time.

| Boundary | Median | Median change | p95 | p95 change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New empty-archive constructor | 24.518 → 4.164 | -83.02% | 27.374 → 6.358 | -76.77% |
| Real CLI --help process | 102.903 → 48.750 | -52.63% | 104.104 → 49.547 | -52.41% |
| Real CLI --version process | 101.346 → 47.479 | -53.15% | 103.116 → 48.259 | -53.20% |
| Full API import, including MemoryBook | 33.506 → 33.920 | +1.24% | 33.822 → 34.433 | +1.81% |
| Existing empty-archive constructor | 0.640 → 0.632 | -1.23% | 0.668 → 0.666 | -0.30% |
| Official SDK transport/server initialization | 627.601 → 620.104 | -1.19% | 632.233 → 624.837 | -1.17% |

New-archive median falls by **20.354 ms**; help and version medians fall by **54.153 ms** and **53.867 ms**. Constructor timing excludes Python launch, import and evidence validation; CLI timing covers the actual complete fresh process; MCP timing ends at successful initialization. These boundaries are separate. All three primary percentage/absolute targets and all six secondary guards pass their preregistered thresholds.

Complete API import becomes slower by **0.414 ms median / 0.611 ms p95**. Existing-archive whole-helper system CPU rises **18.646175 → 21.120575 ms**, or **+2.474400 ms / +13.270282%**, in every round. It is the one pooled resource increase requiring review. Whole-helper wall mean rises **1.233748 ms / 0.889110%**, and saved user+system CPU rises **1.228375 ms**. The existing-archive constructor's own median and p95 do not regress. No syscall/component trace identifies the exact cause; the increase is not dismissed as noise or attributed to the new-schema transaction.

Two independent saved-evidence reviews support accepting this bounded tradeoff for startup scope. The [explicit startup decision](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-decision.json) records that acceptance separately from the unchanged original **`accepted:false` and workflow `failure`**. Every original resource flag and all **6 pooled / 26 round timing increases plus 9 pooled / 27 round resource increases** remain available. Kernel child RSS records and sampled live MCP resources do not establish isolated product-memory savings.

[Full saved-result review](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1-local-audit/review.md) · [Independent resource review](../round6-startup-resource-review.md) · [Original report](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1/report.json.gz) · [Original plan](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-plan.json).

## Retrieval evidence and scope

A's balanced development experiment completed **22,988 calls / 11,494 complete output pairs / 45,976 events** with all complete non-timing outputs equal. Recall improvements were roughly **1%**, insufficient to advance to the original **10% aggregate / 15% public native / 10% actual MCP p95** targets. That four-round formal recall matrix was **not run or accepted**. B regressed public native p95 approximately **19–29%** and actual MCP p95 **23.9246%**; it remains excluded with its entire experiment preserved.

The exact A runtime also matches all **2,304 historical Hotpot256 complete outputs** against v0.3.3, independently audited against **4,608 events**. These are compatibility results, not new retrieval-quality gains. Historical C7 and optional Q2 results retain their original versions and measured boundaries.

## Complete fresh component comparison

The sole [comparison run 43601518020](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43601518020) finished all eight stages: **6,912 retrieval/search calls, 42 quality cells, 13,824 search ledger events and 1,280 separately recorded ai-memory page reads**. All **1,536 native + 768 component complete-output pairs** match v0.3.3; only latency fields are removed for the payload comparison. All 28 original result files match immutable result commit `3e6e492422705feda61b9c967d0a07dd7766dd72`. The [saved-result audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-local-audit.json) reconstructs the original assessment and Markdown exactly, without new product calls.

The same original **256 IDs** exclude all **896 historical IDs with zero overlap**. A unit fixture's manifest-path isolation failure is retained, along with its full ordinary-CI failure logs. The registered [fixture-only recovery](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-comparison-fixture-recovery-addendum.json) preserves all IDs/content hashes and all measurement/packing/adapter logic. It corrects the fixture and records the recovery through separate evaluator, binding and manifest commits before first scoring.

At the common `cl100k_base` 1,024-token whole-block projection, the complete result is:

| Component | Annotation recall | Complete evidence | Packed-context MRR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Book v0.3.3 | 75.93% | 53.12% | 0.8556 |
| Book v0.3.4 | 75.93% | 53.12% | 0.8556 |
| claude-mem 15.18.1 FTS | 70.60% | 48.05% | 0.8060 |
| ai-memory v3.4.5 hybrid | 77.87% | 57.42% | 0.8279 |
| billion-context locked kernel | 80.94% | 60.55% | 0.8481 |

Book exceeds claude-mem's annotation recall and completeness in all six tokenizer/cap cells and has the highest packed-context MRR among the four component implementations in all six. Ai-memory has higher recall and completeness in all six; billion has higher recall in all six and higher completeness at 1,024/2,048 tokens. Book's small 512-token completeness advantage over billion and all per-question losses remain visible. The seven-question low-overlap group also remains: Book completes 0/7, claude-mem 1/7, and ai-memory/billion 2/7 at 512 cl100k tokens. This is **no new retrieval-quality gain against v0.3.3 and no universal competitor lead**.

Fresh timings are descriptive and use a fixed sequential stage order. Five of six native p95 cells increase by **0.23–2.92%**, while o200k/512 decreases **3.39%**; all six native means increase **0.136–3.494%**. Component search p95 increases **3.517899 → 3.582246 ms**, about **1.83%**. Native sampled setup/query RSS increases **547.41 → 551.45 MiB / 533.12 → 537.18 MiB**; component setup wall increases **840.940 → 843.362 ms**. The larger Book native response payload, all repetitions, setup phases, RSS, storage and packing costs remain in the full results. These observations are not dismissed as noise and do not establish a causal recall change from this stage order.

**Provenance clarification beside the [unaltered automatic report](../../benchmarks/results/round6-comparison-43601518020-1/report.md):** its historical renderer text needs two qualifications. Original v1 source/evaluator/assets preceded selection; recovery v2 was frozen after the original selection and before the first scoring. Its historical reference to an ABBA recall release gate does not describe v0.3.4 acceptance: the original 10%/15%/10% recall formal matrix was not run or passed. This release uses the separate prospective startup confirmation. [Recovery freeze audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-recovery-freeze-audit.json) · [Full current comparison guide](../comparison.md) · [Independent fresh review](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-independent-review.json).

These results measure supplied-source evidence on one public answerable cohort, not generated answers, hallucination or abstention, private conversational transfer or whole products. Component API boundaries and setup work differ; no whole-product speed/ingestion/memory ratio follows. Sampled worker-plus-descendant RSS includes the evaluator and dataset, may double-count shared pages and is a lower bound. The original raw tables, source hashes and every adverse result are preserved.

## Release identity and publication gates

The approved publication runtime is **`f361d2bf64a4e1088cbd5cff6ffdaf19aa15e7f1b7ea1de4577d7a488d2ac242`**, byte-identical to source `df35007c29e4af61dd96146232fe4651cfc74391`. The [separate release decision](../../benchmarks/experiments/round6-release-decision.json) preserves the earlier startup decision's historical `publication_approved:false`, the original automatic startup `accepted:false`, the rejected B result and the unpassed recall goals.

The [publication workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/workflows/release.yml) requires the exact final source commit to have all nine CI jobs pass, match `main` and `release/v0.3.4`, and match the approved runtime. It builds and independently installs the wheel and sdist, checks runtime/reader/installer bytes, publishes seven checksummed assets as a normal non-prerelease release, verifies Latest, then installs through the real public URL with default MCP/client extras. Public completion and its verification receipt are recorded after that workflow succeeds; the source-level approval is not itself a claim that those later steps already ran.

[Work and recovery record](../optimization-round6.md) · [Source selection](../../benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-source-selection.json) · [Upgrade guide](../deployment.md#upgrading).

releases.body:
# v0.3.3 — Reduce recall work and MCP output scheduling

AI-Memory-Book keeps original conversation evidence in a shared local archive
for AI clients.

v0.3.3 reduces repeated retrieval work and certified MCP output dispatch
while preserving complete default output. Its fixed numerical performance gates
and final-source historical compatibility checks pass against published v0.3.2.
Three startup costs are accepted through the original plan's independent resource review.

## Changes in this version

- **Combine native MCP output operations once per message.** On the verified
  official SDK 1.30.0 standard-stream path, run the original UTF-8 text write and
  its immediate flush in one default worker dispatch. The paired SDK flush
  acknowledges only that successful operation; independent flushes and failures
  keep the original delegation. The SDK still serializes and frames every
  message, reads stdin, and owns initialization, context and lifespan. No
  response batching, deferred flush or cross-message text buffer is added.
  Unknown SDK versions, replaced/custom methods or unsupported native streams
  use the original FastMCP stdio path. Normal result-cache costs remain intact.
- **Read original source turns together within one snapshot.** For ordinary
  multi-session recalls, a parameterized relation fetches the exact requested
  `(session_pk, ordinal)` pairs through the existing unique index. The batch is
  bounded to 400 pairs / 800 parameters and checked against actual SQLite
  limits. Python 3.10, custom factories, restrictive limits and unsupported or
  malformed inputs retain the original per-session path. Original source-map
  and projected-unit integrity checks remain in the same read transaction.
- **Reuse a captured source-reference parse once.** Final reference projection
  can consume the already parsed map for one ordinary span when the current raw
  reference object and the preparation, JSON and projection methods still
  match. Each page capture is exposed at most once. Multiple spans, repeated
  pages and custom or changed inputs retain the original parsing path, keeping
  `message_indices` and other nested containers independent. No internal fields
  are added to rows or results, and no source map persists across recalls.
- **Read narrow metadata during retrieval.** A covering index on
  `(rid,id,project_id,chapter_id,session_pk)` avoids loading wide page records
  for candidate metadata. Original content and source references remain fetched
  for final results. Unbounded chapter/session routes retain planner choice;
  existing scope predicates, global BM25, ordering and limits stay intact.
- **Read each directory once within a recall.** Candidate pages share chapter
  and session metadata. The new path fetches light candidate addresses and
  then each distinct directory pair once inside the existing read snapshot.
  All referenced rows and field types are checked before pruning; malformed
  metadata and custom factories keep the original path and errors.
- **Skip provably irrelevant scoring.** The existing title multiplier lies
  between 1 and 1.15. A strict score upper bound retains every candidate that
  can enter the original ranking/novelty pool, including ties, while preserving
  the complete original candidate count. Semantic, coverage and custom-callable
  paths remain unpruned. Query-result cache behavior is unchanged; bounded derived count reuse is described below.
- **Avoid repeated Python work.** Identical ordered lexical routes reuse their
  candidate mapping without building unused fusion maps. Native SQLite rows
  feed metadata by position, with the existing custom-row fallback retained.
  Directory overlap is computed once per directory within each recall call.
- **Reuse certified token counts.** Accepted blocks reuse their exact count
  when only a certified ASCII suffix can change after appending a separator.
  The inspected tiktoken 0.12.0 `cl100k_base` and `o200k_base` patterns, encoder
  identity and strict boundary checks remain prerequisites. Unknown patterns,
  custom counters and unsupported text retain full-count fallback behavior.
- **Remember exact counts of repeated evidence blocks.** A lazy memo owned by
  each connection holds at most 2,048 entries and 2 MiB of retained text objects,
  shared by both supported tokenizers. Keys retain the complete original text
  and certified encoder object identity. Unknown/custom implementations use the
  original exact path, and closing the connection releases retained text. The
  text cap excludes container/key/value/encoder overhead; actual RSS is measured
  separately. This is derived counting work, not retrieval-result caching.
- **Reject impossible supplemental pages earlier.** After source-map validation,
  a certified stable citation-header prefix can prove the token budget already
  exhausted, avoiding unnecessary source-unit projection and ranking. Packing
  order, source validation and final exact token counts remain unchanged.
- **Use a 4 MiB SQLite pager target per connection.** `PRAGMA cache_size=-4096`
  sets a connection-local KiB target. It is separate from the query-result cache,
  is not a hard process-memory limit and does not persist a file-format setting.

The derived index is added automatically to existing archives, including after
supported schema migrations, and SQLite maintains it for older/external writers.
Schema 3, source addresses, revision semantics, MCP response formats and product
dependencies remain unchanged. Q2 remains optional; its model and fusion policy
are unchanged. Development alternatives and adverse observations remain in the
[round-five record](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/optimization-round5.md).

The frozen C7 source is
[`d0c84cbfc9bad440ad447d41e211d070ef5b2cae`](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/commit/d0c84cbfc9bad440ad447d41e211d070ef5b2cae),
runtime SHA-256
`55529a217e6dcf6af0c81639cfc0e88b3ea94c39e6911f659fcfb7543e853d45`.

## Verified historical quality compatibility

The final C7 source reproduces **2,304 / 2,304** saved default Book v0.3.2
complete payload hashes on the already scored Hotpot256 cohort: **1,536 native
calls** (two tokenizers, three caps) and **768 component calls**, with zero
mismatches or errors. Only `latency_ms` is excluded. All 4,608 original start /
finish events align with the result rows; source, index and canonical-document
projections remain unchanged and query-result caches stay empty.
[Source-bound compatibility summary](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-hotpot-regression.summary.json)

C3's, C5's and C6's earlier compatibility results remain separately retained
with their original source identities. This C7 check independently preserves the
historical default outputs; it adds no new quality, competitor timing or Q2
evaluation claim. The saved-evidence audit checks all 2,304 result rows and
4,608 original attempt events without issuing further retrieval calls.

## Upgrade and memory costs

The index has storage and first-open costs. An earlier C3 probe of the same
index implementation recorded the following; logical content and revision were
unchanged. These observations retain their C3 source identity:

| Old archive | First open, v0.3.2 → C3, ms | Open + close, ms | Index allocation, bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| synthetic61 | 0.910 → 5.419 | 1.000 → 9.495 | 200,704 |
| public1015 | 0.844 → 4.502 | 0.930 → 7.791 | 151,552 |

Each source/cohort has one sequential observation with warm OS caches; these
are descriptive upgrade costs, not percentiles or a speed acceptance result.
Both copied archives reused free pages, so observed file growth was zero; the
allocated index space is still a cost. The recorded process high-water marks
cannot establish equal live RSS or zero memory overhead.
[Upgrade review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-development/final-index-upgrade-review.json)

A separate baseline-only pager diagnostic observed about **2.1 MiB more process
RSS** at 4 MiB. That observation does not measure final C7 memory use, and its
latency gains cannot be added to the covering-index gains. The rejected 8 MiB
setting and its regression remain in the
[complete cache diagnostic](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-development/sqlite-cache-probe-1/README.md).
Final C7 startup, ingestion, RSS and storage costs are retained in the [formal review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-c7-performance-review.md).

## Formal performance acceptance

The [sole frozen run](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43563390252)
completes **56,784 calls**, four balanced rounds and all **28,392 complete
non-timing output pairs**. All correctness and fixed numerical gates pass.

All fixed numerical gates pass. The original automated verdict remains `accepted:false` because three startup resource increases required review: import means rise 3.197 / 2.990 ms, and public-labeled fresh-empty-database opening rises 5.100 ms (21.4109%). A [separate resource review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-c7-resource-review.md) accepts these startup costs with all samples and attribution limits retained. No timing was repeated, threshold lowered or original automatic verdict rewritten.
The [explicit decision](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/experiments/round5-c7-resource-decision.json) binds the two independent
resource reviews to this exact source and original report.

Pooled p95 geometric mean improves **14.7976%** against published v0.3.2. Public native token512/token1024/token2048 p95 changes **-15.1867% / -14.2362% / -15.7406%**. Actual public SDK MCP token1024 p95 is **6.711 → 5.894 ms**, an improvement of **12.1734%**.

C7 combines the official MCP SDK's native stdout write and immediate flush in one worker dispatch, reducing dispatch overhead while preserving complete messages, serialization and lifecycle.

| Cohort | Configuration | v0.3.2 p95, ms | v0.3.3 p95, ms | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| synthetic61 | native-char4000 | 14.137 | 12.892 | -8.80% |
| synthetic61 | mcp-char4000 | 16.360 | 15.111 | -7.63% |
| synthetic61 | native-token512 | 20.645 | 16.021 | -22.39% |
| synthetic61 | native-token1024 | 21.229 | 14.959 | -29.53% |
| synthetic61 | native-token2048 | 18.307 | 15.383 | -15.97% |
| synthetic61 | mcp-token1024 | 23.597 | 18.107 | -23.27% |
| public1015 | native-char4000 | 3.806 | 3.583 | -5.84% |
| public1015 | mcp-char4000 | 5.740 | 5.580 | -2.79% |
| public1015 | native-token512 | 5.408 | 4.587 | -15.19% |
| public1015 | native-token1024 | 4.599 | 3.945 | -14.24% |
| public1015 | native-token2048 | 4.478 | 3.773 | -15.74% |
| public1015 | mcp-token1024 | 6.711 | 5.894 | -12.17% |

All twelve pooled p50 and p95 values improve. Every per-round observation and all resource comparisons,
including adverse samples, remain in the
[complete review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-c7-performance-review.md).
[Original report](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-performance-43563390252-1/report.json.gz) ·
[Summary](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-performance-43563390252-1/report.summary.json) ·
[Independent arithmetic audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-performance-independent-audit.json) ·
[Frozen saved-ledger audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-performance-local-audit.json).

Query-result caching is disabled or cleared before timing. The registered
derived count memo is enabled: native later token configurations reuse earlier
counts, while each actual SDK MCP configuration starts a fresh server process.
All first calls remain in the samples. MCP timing includes the roundtrip,
serialization and normal server result-cache writes. These repeated old-query
measurements on one host do not establish statistical significance or a
universal speedup. The complete [C3 rejection](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-performance-review.md) and
[C5 rejection](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-c5-performance-review.md) and
[C6 rejection](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/round5-c6-performance-review.md) remain retained.
C5/C6 actual-MCP p95 gains were 6.673181% / 5.798911%, below
10%; both original `accepted:false` decisions are unchanged. All development observations remain retained; neither earlier gains nor old competitor timings supply a
missing gate. [Plan](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/experiments/round5-plan.json) ·
[Frozen binding](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/experiments/round5-c7-performance-binding.json).

## Historical component strengths and limits

The prior supplied-page comparison at 1,024 `cl100k_base` tokens found default
Book complete evidence on **53.91%** of questions versus **44.53%** for
claude-mem 15.18.1 FTS, a **9.375 percentage-point** advantage. ai-memory v3.4.5
and the pinned billion-context kernel had higher recall and completeness;
billion-context also had lower search latency. The final-source C7 regression check
preserves Book's old default outputs. Competitors were not rerun, and old speed
ratios are not v0.3.3 measurements. Different component boundaries also prevent
a whole-product or all-dimensions superiority claim.
[Historical comparison and costs](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/results/round4-comparison-43363060062-1/report.md)

## Install or upgrade

Requires **Python 3.10+ with SQLite FTS5**. The registered publication channel is
a normal [GitHub v0.3.3 release](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/releases/tag/v0.3.3)
(`prerelease=false`), marked Latest on initial publication. Distribution is
through GitHub release assets, not PyPI. The installer uses the release wheel
with MCP/client extras in an isolated environment and preserves the archive.

**macOS / Linux**

```bash
curl -fsSLo install-memory-book.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.3/scripts/install.sh
bash install-memory-book.sh
```

**Windows PowerShell**

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.3/scripts/install.py -OutFile install-memory-book.py
py -3 .\install-memory-book.py
```

Connect a client with `memory-book setup --client claude-code`, then run
`memory-book doctor` and restart the client. Add `--capture --background` to
setup when transcript capture is wanted. Use the installer's full launcher path
if needed. On upgrade, rerun setup with the existing database, clients and
capture options so MCP and any service point to the new environment; the prior
environment is retained. [Deployment and upgrade guide](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/docs/deployment.md#upgrading)

## Release verification

The frozen C7 runtime has [26 directed passing correctness tests](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-correctness.json),
including its new scheduling, cancellation, error, fallback and real-SDK
protocol checks. The overlapping dependency-free invocation executes six of
the same cases and skips twenty; those are not additional unique tests.
The [independent source review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.3/benchmarks/reports/round5-c7-source-review.json)
retains the pre-timing guard corrections and their original evidence.

Publication requires the accepted exact runtime hash, all nine CI jobs on the
final release commit, both package formats matching that source, seven verified
release assets, the normal release channel and a separate public installer
check. Source or development CI does not substitute for final release CI.
Exact release-source, CI-run and asset-verification links are appended by the
publication tooling after the acceptance and packaging gates complete.

# v0.3.2 — Less token-budget work, the same source evidence

The fixed C2 source has passed formal performance acceptance and the complete
fresh component comparison. Independent saved-result audits preserve the gains,
regressions and exact source identities. Publication uses the exact-commit CI
and packaging gates described below.

AI-Memory-Book gives AI clients a shared local archive of original conversations.
This experimental release reduces repeated source parsing and token counting
while preserving the existing retrieval policy, source addresses and budgets.

## Changes in this version

- **Defer unnecessary source parsing.** Capture original turns and source maps
  inside the existing database snapshot. Pages with an affirmative full-segment
  equality certificate need projection only when supplemental evidence is used;
  other maps retain the original eager corruption checks. Deferred work uses
  captured text and performs no later database reads.
- **Narrow projection and reuse accepted work.** Bisection skips source units
  outside a mapped segment while preserving containment and exact-text checks.
  Assembly retains the count for the last accepted context, including when a
  later candidate is rejected, and avoids a redundant private metadata copy.
- **Count certified citation boundaries once per call.** With tiktoken 0.12.0
  and the inspected `cl100k_base`/`o200k_base` patterns, sealed citation blocks
  can reuse exact counts. A strict UTF-8 byte bound can prove that a block fits;
  final `context_tokens` remains exact. Unsupported patterns, custom counters,
  unknown encoder origins and invalid boundaries keep the original full-context
  fallback, including its error behavior.

Global BM25, lexical normalization, ranking, scope filters, packing order,
source coordinates and MCP response formats retain their existing contracts.
Q2's model, vectors and fusion are unchanged. Schema 3 and dependency requirements
are unchanged; no persistent feature cache is added.

The rejected body-feature cache and proposed highlight-query specialization are
absent from C2. Earlier A/B/C1 sources, adverse results and interrupted attempts
remain preserved in the [round-four decision history](../optimization-round4.md).

## Verified compatibility

The completed [Q2 audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/f8f1653c0653654ed574569fff1aaf4dbaeef6d1/benchmarks/reports/round4-compatibility-final/paired-audit.json)
verifies **1,968 calls and 984 matching complete non-latency payload pairs**
against published v0.3.1. It covers authored36 and historical Hotpot128, both
tokenizers and 512/1,024/2,048-token budgets. Baseline and candidate use identical
saved vectors. Recorded source, projection, scope, token and metadata errors
are zero.

These are previously scored regression cohorts. The audit checks recorded
payload hashes, vector/source identities and complete attempt ledgers without
repeating retrieval or inference; it does not establish new quality gains or
independently reconstruct omitted response bodies. Fresh artificial fixtures
cover rejected later blocks, nonmonotonic token counts, Unicode, custom encoders,
source corruption and concurrent writers.

The fixed candidate is
[`2d7b5e38839fb21724ad3beec6b6ebabbda45636`](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/commit/2d7b5e38839fb21724ad3beec6b6ebabbda45636),
runtime SHA-256
`179ab871f4f6ca197efc83b13618cccad4688fd53d4a4af93305b02e78215e93`.
Its [source CI run](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43358743472)
passed all nine jobs. Final release verification remains separate.

## Completed formal performance

The sole registered hosted run was triggered from
[`f8f1653c0653654ed574569fff1aaf4dbaeef6d1`](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/f8f1653c0653654ed574569fff1aaf4dbaeef6d1/benchmarks/experiments/round4-performance-binding.json).
Its completed matrix has **56,784 calls**, sixteen sequential workers, four
balanced rounds and twelve cohort/configuration cells, including actual SDK
MCP. Complete outputs and recorded invariants match. The original automatic
verdict is **accepted**, with no resource exception or gate change.

Across the twelve pooled cells, the geometric-mean p95 improvement is **10.13%**.
The following public-corpus cells each contain 4,060 samples per source:

| Configuration | v0.3.1 p95, ms | v0.3.2 p95, ms | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native, 4,000 characters | 2.361 | 2.199 | −6.89% |
| Actual SDK MCP, 4,000 characters | 3.468 | 3.518 | **+1.44%** |
| Native, 512 tokens | 3.794 | 3.070 | −19.07% |
| Native, 1,024 tokens | 3.200 | 2.611 | −18.41% |
| Native, 2,048 tokens | 3.130 | 2.560 | −18.20% |
| Actual SDK MCP, 1,024 tokens | 4.358 | 3.887 | −10.80% |

No pooled p50/p95 regression exceeds 5%. The largest registered resource mean
increase is **6.02%**, public token-MCP startup from 345.683 to 366.504 ms.
All round-level regressions and raw samples remain published. The aggregate
exceeds its 10% gate by only **0.1294 percentage points**; these descriptive
results establish neither statistical significance nor a universal speedup.
Returned text and output-token totals are unchanged, so this release does not
claim model-token savings from this optimization.

[Full evidence](../../benchmarks/reports/round4-performance-43361086255-1/report.json.gz) ·
[Summary](../../benchmarks/reports/round4-performance-43361086255-1/report.summary.json) ·
[Independent performance and resource review](../round4-performance-review.md) ·
[Independent arithmetic audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round4-performance-independent-audit.json)

## Completed fresh component comparison

The frozen selection contains **256 questions**, **635 evidence annotations**
and **2,548 context paragraphs**, with zero overlap against all **640** prior
question IDs. Source, evaluator, dependency, model and component identities
were committed before the salted ID selection. An independent ID-only audit
reproduces the exact order and verifies the binding/manifest commit sequence.
The single ten-stage scoring run completed **4,608 native calls and 4,608
component searches**. All 54 quality cells pass integrity checks, and the
1,536 native / 768 component default-payload pairs match. The unchanged strict
verifier exactly reproduces the saved assessment and report; separate arithmetic
checks 13,824 quality rows and all 18,432 attempt events without new retrieval.

The common view below uses supplied source pages, top five and a whole-page
packer at **1,024 `cl100k_base` tokens**. Search p95 pools three repetitions.

| Component | Evidence recall | Complete evidence | Packed MRR | Search-adapter p95, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Book, default lexical | 75.75% | 53.91% | 0.8578 | 3.488 |
| Book, optional Q2 | 76.69% | 55.08% | **0.8663** | 20.406 |
| claude-mem 15.18.1 FTS | 70.39% | 44.53% | 0.8280 | 34.655 |
| ai-memory v3.4.5 hybrid | 77.48% | 55.86% | 0.8400 | 39.925 |
| billion-context 9674cfa kernel | **80.94%** | **60.55%** | 0.8606 | **1.449** |

Default Book has **9.375 percentage points** higher complete evidence than
claude-mem FTS here. Its measured search-adapter p95 is **89.94% lower than
claude-mem's and 91.26% lower than ai-memory's**. These are different Python,
SQLite/Bun, HTTP/MCP and Node component boundaries, so they do not establish
whole-product ratios. ai-memory and billion-context retain higher recall and
completeness; billion-context's kernel is faster. Q2 leads packed MRR in this
slice, with 26 complete-question gains and 23 losses over default at this cap.

Q2 remains opt-in. Native 512-token completeness falls from **39.45% to 36.33%**
with cl100k and to **36.72%** with o200k. Its fresh native total setup takes
282.970 s, including ingestion, model loading and index construction, versus
lexical setup 3.796 s. The separate model cache adds 127,535,388 bytes.
All query, preparation, read, payload and storage costs are retained.

The fresh **100,000-character component** path also has a retained regression
against v0.3.1: p95 **3.304 → 3.488 ms (+5.56%)**, p50 **+5.12%**, and sampled
setup process-tree RSS **548.65 → 943.53 MiB (+71.97%)**. Native lexical
finalization RSS rises **655.16 → 1,107.09 MiB**. These sequential, unbalanced
observations include evaluator/data memory and may double-count shared pages;
the cause is not established. They remain separate from the formal balanced
performance gate and its resource means.

The source remains public HotpotQA; it is not a new domain. All questions are
answerable, and this is evidence retrieval rather than generated-answer or
hallucination evaluation. Historical reports retain their original identities.
[Full comparison](../../benchmarks/results/round4-comparison-43363060062-1/report.md) ·
[Independent audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round4-comparison-independent-audit.json) ·
[Costs and all tradeoffs](../comparison.md) ·
[Frozen manifest](../../benchmarks/experiments/round4-hotpot256-manifest.json) ·
[Independent freeze audit](../../benchmarks/reports/round4-freeze-independent-audit.json)

Requires **Python 3.10+ with SQLite FTS5**. The installer uses the small v0.3.2

MCP/client imports. See the [release checkpoint](../round4-continuation.md) for
the final recorded publication and installation outcome.

This remains an experimental local single-user project. Client configuration
fixtures do not certify every vendor application's interactive behavior. The

# v0.3.1 — Faster scoped recall, the same original evidence

AI-Memory-Book gives AI clients a shared local archive of original conversations.
This experimental release reduces work inside project-scoped SQLite queries,
preserves the default retrieval output, and keeps the small-wheel installer and
one-command MCP setup.

## Verified changes

The registered comparison against v0.3.0 completed **47,320 calls**, covering
two old corpora, five native/MCP and character/token configurations, and four
balanced rounds. Complete non-timing outputs matched. Across the ten pooled
cohort/configuration cells, the geometric mean of p95 improves **11.36%**.

| Public-conversation setting | v0.3.0 p95 | v0.3.1 p95 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native recall, 4,000 characters | 5.054 ms | 3.737 ms | **−26.05%** |
| Actual SDK MCP stdio, 4,000 characters | 7.409 ms | 5.937 ms | **−19.87%** |

These figures use the same 1,015 questions and host, with no reuse of cached
recall results. OS/SQLite caches warm naturally; this is not an OS-cold-cache
measurement. The optimization narrows FTS iteration only
when a project's rowid span is at most half the archive's span; other requests
retain the original plan. Exact scope predicates still apply before the
candidate limit, and global BM25, ranking, source addresses and budget handling
stay intact.

**The tradeoffs remain visible.** A synthetic 512-token configuration has
**0.125% higher p95**. The public workers' mean fresh empty-database opening time increases from
**34.456 to 39.294 ms**, a **4.838 ms / 14.04%** cost. Independent review explicitly
accepted that startup tradeoff. The original automated report remains
`accepted: false` because it required that review; no sample was removed and
the original gate result was not rewritten.

[Performance and resource review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/docs/round3-performance-review.md) ·
[Machine-readable review](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/benchmarks/reports/round3-recovery/performance-resource-review.json) ·
[Original performance run](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/actions/runs/43246417515) ·
[Immutable original results and ledgers](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/tree/35b8618a078fe377ecd6c5acc331c1281dbf61e7/benchmarks/reports/round3-performance-43246417515-1)

## Current component comparison

The completed [new-256 report](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/c99f20531053b1c164fc5a5d3fa8e0c831eeb4de/benchmarks/results/round3-comparison-43267797247-1/report.md)
uses another fixed HotpotQA selection, with **zero overlap with the 384 earlier
question IDs**. Source, model, dependency and evaluator identities were committed
before selection. **4,608 native calls and 4,608 component searches** pass the
registered integrity checks. Complete default payloads match v0.3.0 across
**1,536 native pairs and 768 component pairs**, after removing only `latency_ms`.

The following slice uses the same supplied pages, top five results and common
whole-block packing at **1,024 `cl100k_base` tokens**:

| Measured component | Evidence recall | Complete evidence | Packed MRR | Mean context tokens | Search adapter p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Book v0.3.1 · default lexical | 76.28% | 52.34% | 0.8132 | 719.8 | 2.784 ms |
| Book v0.3.1 · optional Q2 | 76.77% | 54.69% | 0.8239 | 739.0 | 11.226 ms |
| claude-mem 15.18.1 · native FTS | 70.68% | 45.31% | 0.7674 | 715.8 | 22.826 ms |
| ai-memory v3.4.5 · local hybrid | 77.27% | 55.86% | 0.8182 | 716.8 | 27.545 ms |
| billion-context `9674cfa` · search kernel | **78.91%** | **58.20%** | **0.8277** | 762.3 | **1.010 ms** |

Default Book completeness is **7.03 percentage points above claude-mem FTS**
in this slice. Optional Q2 adds **2.34 percentage points** over Book lexical,
but **ai-memory retains higher recall and completeness**. **billion-context
leads these three quality metrics and search latency.** Book's advantage over
claude-mem and ai-memory here is lower measured search-adapter latency, alongside
its default model-free local archive and evidence path.

These adapters have different boundaries: Book runs in-process Python including
context assembly; claude-mem uses SQLite/Bun; ai-memory uses local HTTP/MCP; and
billion-context runs a locked supplied-source search kernel in Node. Their
timings do not establish whole-product speed ratios. ai-memory's first search
plus all source reads has p95 **30.532 ms**, versus its **27.545 ms** search-only
p95. Search/read payload tokens, packed-context tokens, setup/index time, state
size and sampled process memory are separate measurements in the full report.

**Q2 remains optional.** At native 512-token limits, complete evidence falls
from **35.94% to 33.59%** with `cl100k_base`, and from **35.55% to 33.20%** with
`o200k_base`. Q2 also incurs model/index setup, memory and query costs. In the
six-question low-lexical-overlap group at 512 `cl100k_base` tokens, both Book
modes still find complete evidence for **zero of six** questions. These small
diagnostics do not establish a solution to low-overlap retrieval.

All selected questions are answerable, and all come from the same public
HotpotQA source. Cross-session/chapter labels reflect supplied encyclopedia
paragraphs mapped into archive structure; they do not measure private
conversation transfer. This evaluates returned source evidence, not generated
answer accuracy, abstention, hallucinations or a complete write/summarize/generate
workflow. Per-question gains and losses, every budget and both tokenizers remain
in the [machine-readable assessment](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/c99f20531053b1c164fc5a5d3fa8e0c831eeb4de/benchmarks/results/round3-comparison-43267797247-1/assessment.json).
These question IDs became regression data after their first scoring.

## A rejected candidate stays out of the product

The optional project-local FTS statistics experiment was interrupted during
evidence transfer. Its **eight workers and 8,082 calls** have been restored and
audited with **zero retrieval replays**. The restored aggregate matches the
original recorded byte identities and saved prefixes. **Fourteen loss checks**
reject it under its registered screen, so it is not included in the product or
the new comparison's accepted configurations.

The default remains global-statistics lexical retrieval. Q2 semantics, exact
token caps, multi-fact coverage and indexed MCP references remain explicit
options with their documented costs and losses. Book's Q2 initialization now
sets the ONNX Runtime telemetry opt-out before import and also disables telemetry
through the runtime API.

[Independent recovery verification](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/benchmarks/reports/round3-recovery/quality-cross-verification.json) ·
[Original round-three plan](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/2ce405408d323aac61fa9e9f536a704dd5f2b372/benchmarks/experiments/round3-plan.json) ·
[Local semantic retrieval](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/docs/semantic-retrieval.md)

## Install or upgrade

Requires **Python 3.10+ with SQLite FTS5**. The installer uses the release's small
universal wheel in an isolated environment with MCP/client dependencies. Git,
Node.js and a separate database server are not needed for normal use.

**macOS / Linux**

```bash
curl -fsSLo install-memory-book.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.1/scripts/install.sh
bash install-memory-book.sh
```

**Windows PowerShell**

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.1/scripts/install.py -OutFile install-memory-book.py
py -3 .\install-memory-book.py
```

Connect your client and explicitly enable supported transcript capture:

```bash
memory-book setup --client claude-code --capture --background
memory-book doctor
```

Use the full launcher path printed by the installer if it is not on PATH, then
restart the client. Replace `claude-code` with a supported profile; omit
`--capture` for MCP access alone. Host permissions and model tool selection
still determine whether memory is called.

To upgrade, re-run the installer and the same `setup` command so MCP and the
background service use the new environment. The archive and previous environment
are retained. This release keeps schema 3; the
[upgrade guide](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/docs/deployment.md#upgrading) explains older-schema upgrades and
rollback requirements.

[English quick start](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/README.md) · [中文快速开始](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/README.zh-CN.md) ·
[Client profiles](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.1/docs/integrations.md#supported-profiles)

## Verify the recorded measurements

With Python 3.12 and this checkout's original evaluator files, audit the

# v0.3.0 — Faster local memory, smaller MCP responses

AI-Memory-Book gives agents a shared local archive of original evidence. This
experimental release packages the verified retrieval, context-budget and MCP
improvements with a shorter setup path and concise English/Chinese documentation.

## Highlights

- **Lightweight default:** Python + SQLite memory writing and lexical retrieval,
  zero model calls, original source references and project/task/session scopes.
- **Faster identical-output recall:** actual MCP pooled p95 falls **1.25%–9.50%**
  in four balanced rounds; public-corpus ingestion time falls **46.45%** and
  unchanged-session replay time **61.38%**. The full non-timing payload is preserved.
- **Optional smaller references:** `memory-book mcp --source-format indexed`
  preserves evidence and reconstructs every source field. At the documented
  1,015-question public / 4,000-character / compact / `o200k_base` setting,
  response-text tokens fall **19.63%** and the first-call reference total **8.15%**.
  The latter includes schema, initialization instructions and arguments.
- **Explicit quality/budget options:** exact named-tokenizer context limits,
  local Q2 semantic fusion and multi-fact coverage; the default remains lexical.
- **Simpler deployment:** installers now use the v0.3.0 universal wheel instead
  of downloading the repository's benchmark history. MCP/client extras are
  included; Git, Node.js and a separate database server are not needed.

## Current comparison

On the same-host, 256-question HotpotQA component comparison with a common
1,024-token `cl100k_base` whole-page packer, Q2 complete evidence is **57.81%**,
versus **48.83%** for claude-mem 15.18.1 FTS and **53.91%** for ai-memory v3.4.5
local hybrid. Book's default lexical component has **8.301 ms p95**; Q2 has
**22.523 ms**, compared with **29.948 ms** and **33.251 ms** for those two
components. Interfaces differ, so these are not whole-product speed ratios.
The billion-context kernel leads this slice's completeness (**61.72%**),
evidence recall and search latency.

[Full comparison, costs and scope](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/docs/comparison.md) ·
[Default performance](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/docs/default-recall-performance.md) ·
[Indexed references](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/docs/indexed-references.md)

## Install and connect

Requires Python 3.10+ with SQLite FTS5.

**macOS / Linux**

```bash
curl -fsSLo install-memory-book.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.0/scripts/install.sh
bash install-memory-book.sh
```

**Windows PowerShell**

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.0/scripts/install.py -OutFile install-memory-book.py
py -3 .\install-memory-book.py
```

Then connect a client and explicitly enable supported transcript capture:

```bash
memory-book setup --client claude-code --capture --background
memory-book doctor
```

Use the exact launcher path printed by the installer if it is not on PATH, then
restart the client. Replace `claude-code` with your supported profile; omit
`--capture` for MCP access alone. Host permissions and model tool selection apply.

**Upgrade:** re-run the installer and the same `setup` command so client and
background-service paths use the new environment. The installer retains existing
memory and the previous environment. The source-preserving schema upgrade runs
when the new engine opens an older archive. Older v0.1 working-directory databases
are not moved automatically. Back up an existing database before upgrading:
schema 3 has no automatic downgrade, and older binaries require the pre-upgrade
database backup for rollback.

[English quick start](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/README.md) ·
[中文快速开始与流程图](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/README.zh-CN.md) ·
[Deployment and upgrades](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/v0.3.0/docs/deployment.md)

## Validation and remaining limits

The release requires all nine exact-commit CI jobs: Python 3.10/3.12/3.13,
actual MCP stdio, the reader browser, Linux/macOS/Windows installers and container
persistence. Published assets include wheel/source distributions, installers,
checksums and source/build provenance; the exact CI run is linked below. The repository retains original measurement
files, negative experiments and independent audit records.

Q2 adds local model/index costs and can lose evidence at small budgets: native
completeness at 512 `o200k_base` tokens / 8,000 characters is **42.19% lexical →
41.02% Q2**. Sparse indexed references can add tokens; the displayed p95 changes
from **7.126 to 7.131 ms**, with no format speedup claim. Reference-token counts
are not provider billing. Public/reused data are regression evidence, and the
current component scores are not final-answer accuracy or proof of cross-domain
transfer. Earlier generated-answer/workflow diagnostics retain their own source
and model settings. The rejected capped-novelty candidate is not included.

This remains an experimental, local single-user project. Client configuration
fixtures do not certify every vendor app; automatic invocation is not guaranteed.
The local archive is unencrypted, and recalled evidence enters the AI client's
model context.

The local suite passed 159 tests with MCP and client extras. ## Verification

The final main commit `e7c60c4` passed all nine CI jobs: Python 3.10/3.12/3.13 core checks, 158 tests with MCP/client extras, real browser interactions, Linux/macOS/Windows installer and recovery checks, and Docker MCP/reader/persistence checks.

See the [English README](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book#readme), [deployment guide](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/main/docs/deployment.md), and [client compatibility](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/blob/main/docs/integrations.md).

把项目变成书，把任务变成章，把会话变成节。一次检索，直接返回带出处的记忆页。首个实验性开源版本，采用 MIT 许可证。

- CLI、Python API、官方 SDK 的 stdio MCP；默认六个只读工具，写入需显式开启。
- canonical JSON、ChatGPT 当前分支、Claude Code JSONL、Codex JSONL 文本导入；规范化 JSON 和 Markdown 记忆书导出。
- 中英文文档、合成示例、可复现实验及完整逐查询数据。

- 83 项 unittest；GitHub CI 覆盖 Python 3.10 / 3.12 / 3.13 和真实 MCP stdio 客户端。
- 真实 Chrome 测试通过桌面与 390px 手机布局、中文搜索、目录、原文、导入流程、焦点恢复与页面错误检查；截图和 JSON 报告保存在 docs/assets。

# AI-Memory-Book

**Give your AI agents a shared local memory, with original evidence they can cite.**

Projects become books, tasks become chapters, and earlier decisions stay available across sessions and clients. One MCP call returns relevant evidence within a context budget so the agent can continue your work.

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Measured results](#measured-results) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [v0.3.4 release](https://github.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/releases/tag/v0.3.4)

**v0.3.4 · Faster initialization and CLI startup · MIT · Python 3.10+ · Local SQLite**

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    H["Supported conversations"] -->|"Opt-in capture or import"| B["Local archive: original text + source addresses"]
    T["An agent needs earlier work"] -->|"One scoped MCP recall"| R["Query + project scope"]
    B --> R
    R --> L["Default: local lexical search"]
    R -.-> S["Optional: Q2 lexical + semantic fusion"]
    L --> E["Evidence within budget + citations"]
    S --> E
    E --> A["Your AI model continues the task"]
```

Capture updates the archive independently of retrieval. The agent can recall directly, then open an exact source page when it needs more detail; browsing the book hierarchy is optional. [Agent workflow](docs/agent-guide.md).

## Why use it?

- **Lightweight by default.** Memory writing and lexical retrieval use zero model calls. The core needs Python and SQLite, with no embedding download, database server, or memory-service API key.
- **Evidence you can inspect.** Preserve original text, project/session/turn references and exact source spans. Character limits are built in; optional named-tokenizer limits also count citations and separators.
- **One archive across clients.** MCP configuration profiles cover Claude Code/Desktop, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and more. Explicitly enabled background capture keeps supported transcripts current; the worker is headless by default.
- **Measured startup improvements.** v0.3.4 reduces fresh-archive initialization and CLI help/version startup time while preserving complete retrieval outputs. Import and retrieval costs remain disclosed below; optional indexed references retain their separate historical token-format results.

## Quick start

You need **Python 3.10+ with SQLite FTS5**. The installer downloads the release wheel into an isolated environment with MCP/client dependencies. No Git checkout or Node.js is needed.

**macOS / Linux**

```bash
curl -fsSLo install-memory-book.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.4/scripts/install.sh
bash install-memory-book.sh
```

**Windows PowerShell**

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Afloat16/AI-Memory-Book/v0.3.4/scripts/install.py -OutFile install-memory-book.py
py -3 .\install-memory-book.py
```

**Connect your agent**

```bash
memory-book setup --client claude-code --capture --background
memory-book doctor
```

Use the launcher's full path printed by the installer if `memory-book` is not yet on your PATH. Restart the client, then ask: **“Recall our earlier decision about this task, cite the source, and continue.”**

Replace `claude-code` with your [client profile](docs/integrations.md#supported-profiles), or repeat `--client` to share the archive across clients. `--capture` opts in to existing and future supported text transcripts; omit it for MCP access alone. Native capture covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and legacy Python Kimi; other profiles use explicit imports or enabled MCP writing. Host permissions and model tool selection still apply.

**Upgrading?** Re-run the installer, then your `setup` command with the same clients and capture options so MCP and any background service use the new environment. Existing memory and the previous environment are retained. [Upgrade details](docs/deployment.md#upgrading).

## Measured results

### v0.3.4: faster initialization and CLI startup

**v0.3.4 creates an empty archive much faster and halves CLI help/version startup time against v0.3.3.** The single prospective confirmation completed **480 fresh samples**, with **40 per version and boundary**, in four balanced AB/BA/BA/AB rounds on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12. All fixed numerical startup gates pass. A [separate explicit decision](benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-decision.json) accepts the one disclosed resource cost under the original review policy; the saved automatic result remains `accepted:false` and the original workflow remains `failure`. [Registered plan](benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-plan.json) · [Original report](benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1/report.json.gz) · [Independent saved-result review](benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1-local-audit/review.md).

All times are milliseconds. Each arrow is **v0.3.3 → v0.3.4**; negative changes are improvements.

| Measured boundary | Median | Median change | p95 | p95 change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Construct a new empty archive** | **24.518 → 4.164** | **−83.02%** | **27.374 → 6.358** | **−76.77%** |
| **Actual CLI `--help` process** | **102.903 → 48.750** | **−52.63%** | **104.104 → 49.547** | **−52.41%** |
| **Actual CLI `--version` process** | **101.346 → 47.479** | **−53.15%** | **103.116 → 48.259** | **−53.20%** |
| Complete API import, including `MemoryBook` | 33.506 → 33.920 | **+1.24%** | 33.822 → 34.433 | **+1.81%** |
| Construct a connection to an existing empty archive | 0.640 → 0.632 | −1.23% | 0.668 → 0.666 | −0.30% |
| Official SDK MCP startup through initialization | 627.601 → 620.104 | −1.19% | 632.233 → 624.837 | −1.17% |

New-archive construction saves **20.354 ms** at the median; CLI help and version save **54.153 ms** and **53.867 ms**. The API constructor timers exclude Python/import and helper validation; CLI values include the actual fresh process and captured output. MCP values start before transport/server creation and end at successful initialization. They are different boundaries, not interchangeable whole-product startup times. No first sample or outlier was removed. All **960 intent/completion events** and original source/evaluator identities passed independent offline verification.

The implementation puts **initial schema and FTS setup in one transaction**, with rollback if that setup fails. Subsequent covering-index and connection-setting steps retain their existing boundaries. Command metadata is loaded without importing archive/client machinery; requesting the public `MemoryBook` class still performs the full API import. Existing archives, schema 3, class identity and complete retrieval output are preserved.

**The costs remain visible.** Full API import is slower by **0.414 ms median / 0.611 ms p95**. Existing-archive whole-helper system CPU rises **18.646 → 21.121 ms (+2.474 ms, +13.2703%)**, the sole pooled resource-review trigger; whole-helper wall time rises **138.762 → 139.996 ms (+0.8891%)** even though its constructor interval improves slightly. The increase occurs in all four rounds. Saved data cannot quantify how much belongs to imports, validation, serialization or other phases. Two independent reviews assessed the disclosed cost and its attribution limits. The [explicit startup decision](benchmarks/experiments/round6-startup-decision.json) accepts it under the original resource policy, with no repeated timing or changed raw verdict. [Resource assessment](docs/round6-startup-resource-review.md). Publication has separate final-CI, package and public-installer gates; their evidence belongs in the [release record](docs/releases/v0.3.4.md).

<details>
<summary>All pooled resource increases and retained adverse observations</summary>

CPU and wall values below are means in milliseconds; RSS values are mean kernel records in KiB. The review also retains every positive and negative per-round cell.

| Boundary and resource | v0.3.3 → v0.3.4 | Increase |
|---|---:|---:|
| API import: whole-helper system CPU | 18.727 → 19.576 ms | +4.5343% |
| API import: kernel maximum-RSS record | 49,221.4 → 49,243.8 KiB | +0.0455% |
| New archive: whole-helper user CPU | 120.770 → 121.288 ms | +0.4289% |
| New archive: kernel maximum-RSS record | 49,460.1 → 49,496.3 KiB | +0.0732% |

The complete record contains **6 pooled timing increases, 26 round timing increases, 9 pooled resource increases and 27 round resource increases**. Beyond the import median/p95 above, import mean/minimum/maximum rise **1.4785% / 1.3192% / 4.2380%**; the existing-archive constructor maximum rises **0.672010 → 0.703721 ms (+4.7188%)**. Round-level increases include API-import system CPU **+13.8606%** and sampled MCP-server system CPU **+15.00%**. The original review rule applies to pooled resource means; none of these observations was discarded. [Every adverse cell](benchmarks/reports/round6-startup-43598913606-1-local-audit/review.json).

Both sources' new/existing logical archives are **159,744 bytes**. Kernel `wait4` RSS records include the measurement process and can include inherited/reaped-descendant effects; they do not establish equal or lower isolated product memory. MCP RSS/HWM and CPU are live samples after initialization, not unobserved lifetime maxima or totals.

</details>

### Retrieval compatibility and release scope

v0.3.4 covers **startup performance and initialization correctness**. Candidate A's two-round development recall gains were approximately **1%**, insufficient to advance to the original **10% aggregate / 15% public native-token / 10% actual-MCP p95** goals. That four-round formal recall matrix was **not run or accepted**. Candidate B's dense-project ranking regressed public native p95 by roughly **19–29%** and actual-MCP p95 by **23.9246%**; it is excluded. v0.3.4 uses A's exact runtime, and all failed experiments remain available. [Development outcomes and source selection](docs/optimization-round6.md).

A preserves **2,304 / 2,304** complete historical Hotpot256 default outputs against v0.3.3: **1,536 native** calls across two tokenizers and three caps, plus **768 component** calls. Its independent saved-ledger audit checks **4,608 events**. This is compatibility evidence, not a new evidence-quality or recall-speed claim. [Historical compatibility](benchmarks/reports/round6-hotpot-compatibility.summary.json) · [Saved-output audit](benchmarks/reports/round6-hotpot-compatibility.audit.json).

**Historical results remain historical.** v0.3.3's accepted C7 comparison against v0.3.2 recorded **14.80% aggregate p95** and **12.17% actual-MCP token p95** improvements, with separately reviewed startup costs. Those values are not v0.3.4 gains and are not added to the new startup percentages. [Original v0.3.3 performance and costs](docs/round5-c7-performance-review.md) · [Resource decision](benchmarks/experiments/round5-c7-resource-decision.json) · [Earlier rejected candidates](docs/optimization-round5.md). Optional indexed references retain their separate, unremeasured [historical token-format results](docs/indexed-references.md).

### Fresh open-source component comparison

The completed comparison uses **256 fresh HotpotQA questions**, excluding all **896 historical IDs** with zero overlap, and **619 required evidence annotations**. It retains **42 quality cells**, **6,912 retrieval/search calls** (3,072 native and 3,840 component searches), plus **1,280 separately counted ai-memory page reads**. All **1,536 native and 768 component complete-output pairs** match between v0.3.3 and v0.3.4 after removing the measured `latency_ms` field. Retrieval quality is unchanged between these Book versions. Q2 and project-statistics ranking are excluded. [Original full report](benchmarks/results/round6-comparison-43601518020-1/report.md) · [Machine-readable assessment](benchmarks/results/round6-comparison-43601518020-1/assessment.json) · [Saved-ledger and identity audit](benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-local-audit.json) · [Independent review and every adverse observation](benchmarks/reports/round6-comparison-43601518020-1-independent-review.json).

**Two legacy sentences in the saved report need this provenance context.** The original v1 source/evaluator freeze preceded selection. The fixture-only v2 recovery was frozen **after the same 256 IDs were fixed, before their first scoring**, with no reselection or scored rerun. Its sentence assigning the release gate to an old-data ABBA recall experiment does **not** describe v0.3.4 acceptance: the original **10% / 15% / 10% recall formal matrix was not run or accepted**. The separate prospective startup experiment above supplies this version's confirmed performance improvement. The original report remains unchanged. [Recovery registration](benchmarks/experiments/round6-comparison-fixture-recovery-addendum.json) · [Exact recovery binding](benchmarks/experiments/round6-comparison-recovery-binding.json).

The table uses the same supplied pages, top five results and common whole-block packing at **1,024 `cl100k_base` tokens**. External components are the locked revisions shown, not a claim about their latest releases.

| Measured component (pinned version) | Evidence recall | Complete evidence | Packed MRR | Mean context tokens | Search adapter p95 |

| Book v0.3.3 · default lexical | 75.93% | 53.12% | 0.8556 | 715.5 | 3.518 ms |

| billion-context `9674cfa` · search kernel | 80.94% | 60.55% | 0.8481 | 760.4 | 1.399 ms |

Book has **5.0781 percentage points higher complete-evidence rate than claude-mem** here, with **24 question gains and 11 losses**, and the highest packed MRR, tied across the two Book versions. Its search-adapter p95 is lower than claude-mem's and ai-memory's. **ai-memory exceeds Book's recall and completeness; billion-context leads recall, completeness and measured search latency.** Book trails their completeness by **4.2969** and **7.4219 percentage points**, respectively. These results establish specific component advantages and disadvantages, without an overall winner.

Search p95 pools all three searches per question and excludes offline common packing and additional page reads. Book uses in-process Python recall and context assembly; claude-mem uses SQLite/Bun, ai-memory local hybrid HTTP/MCP, and billion-context its supplied-source search kernel/Node. These different boundaries do not establish whole-product speed ratios. ai-memory's first search plus all five reads has p95 **46.338 ms**, compared with its search-only **40.409 ms**.
